I also constantly find myself asking my roommate or mom for reassurance about whether I look weird.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe there is a real flaw in your appearance that others can see, or do you worry that your concern may be excessive or not fully accurate?\n\nPatient: To me, the flaws feel completely real and obvious—all I see in photos is how huge and crooked my nose is and how uneven my skin looks. Even though my family and coworkers tell me I look fine and don't notice anything, I still can't stop zooming in and fixating on it. It leaves me feeling really stuck between what I see so clearly and what everyone else tells me.\n\nDoctor: When you think about your nose or skin, do you ever believe with complete certainty that there is a real defect, or do you recognize that this concern might be exaggerated or mainly in your mind?\n\nPatient: When I'm looking at a photo, I honestly believe with complete certainty that the defects are real because they are just so obvious to me. It's incredibly hard to think it's all in my mind when I can see my crooked nose right there on the screen. Even if I try to tell myself it might be exaggerated, in those moments, it feels one hundred percent real.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever hear, see, or strongly believe things about your appearance that other people say are not true, such as being watched, talked about, or targeted because of your looks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like people are watching me, talking about me, or targeting me because of how I look. My focus is purely on how bad I think I look in photos and in the mirror, and even though my mom and roommate tell me they don't notice anything wrong, I still strongly believe my nose is huge and crooked and my skin is uneven.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had other unusual beliefs, like being watched, followed, or harmed because of your appearance, or is the concern limited only to your looks and photos?\n\nPatient: No, I have never believed that I was being watched, followed, or harmed in any way. My concerns are strictly limited to my physical appearance and how bad I look in photos.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, such as hearing or seeing things that others do not, or feeling that people are trying to harm or control you?\n\nPatient: No, I have never experienced hearing or seeing things that others do not. I've also never felt like anyone was trying to harm or control me in any way.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think there is a chance your concern about your appearance could be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain the defect is real even when others disagree?\n\nPatient: I feel completely certain that the flaws are real, because when I look in the mirror or at photos, the crookedness of my nose and my uneven skin are just so glaringly obvious. Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers tell me I look fine and that they don't notice anything, I honestly can't believe they don't see it too.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been able to consider that your appearance concerns might be a false belief or an exaggeration, or are you completely unable to doubt them even a little?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure. It feels so completely real to me when I look at photos that I haven't ever thought about it being a false belief or an exaggeration.\n\nDoctor: When you are not looking at photos or in the mirror, do you ever think there is a chance that your appearance concerns might be exaggerated or untrue, or do you stay completely convinced even then?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't really thought about it in those terms, because the worry about how I look is just always there in the back of my mind.\n\nDoctor: When you are not checking mirrors or photos, can you ever recognize that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or are you completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure and I haven't really thought about it that way. But whenever I do look at myself, the flaws feel completely real and it's just very distressing.\n\nDoctor: When you are not looking in mirrors or photos, can you ever think that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or are you completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?\n\nPatient: I'm still not really sure how to answer that, because I haven't really thought about whether my concerns are exaggerated when I'm not looking at a screen or mirror. I just know that whenever I do see myself, it feels incredibly real and distressing.\n\nDoctor: Outside of looking in mirrors or photos, can you ever recognize that your concern about your appearance might be exaggerated, or do you stay completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?\n\nPatient: It honestly feels completely real to me all the time, and I find it hard to believe otherwise. Even though others try to reassure me and say they don't notice anything, my huge, crooked nose and uneven skin just look so obvious and terrible to me that I stay convinced the flaws are real.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought that other people might be seeing your appearance differently than you do, or do you believe with complete certainty that the flaw is real and obvious to everyone?\n\nPatient: Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers constantly tell me I look fine and that they don't notice anything wrong, I still feel completely convinced that the flaws are real. Or is it mainly a preoccupation with how you look in photos?\n\nPatient: No, it's not really about washing or counting things—it's entirely focused on how I look. I feel driven to do things like taking dozens of selfies to check my angles, zooming in on pictures, and redoing my makeup and outfits over and over to hide my nose and skin. I also constantly find myself asking my roommate or mom for reassurance about whether I look weird.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe there is a real flaw in your appearance that others can see, or do you worry that your concern may be excessive or not fully accurate?\n\nPatient: To me, the flaws feel completely real and obvious—all I see in photos is how huge and crooked my nose is and how uneven my skin looks. Even though my family and coworkers tell me I look fine and don't notice anything, I still can't stop zooming in and fixating on it. It leaves me feeling really stuck between what I see so clearly and what everyone else tells me.\n\nDoctor: When you think about your nose or skin, do you ever believe with complete certainty that there is a real defect, or do you recognize that this concern might be exaggerated or mainly in your mind?\n\nPatient: When I'm looking at a photo, I honestly believe with complete certainty that the defects are real because they are just so obvious to me. It's incredibly hard to think it's all in my mind when I can see my crooked nose right there on the screen. Even if I try to tell myself it might be exaggerated, in those moments, it feels one hundred percent real.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever hear, see, or strongly believe things about your appearance that other people say are not true, such as being watched, talked about, or targeted because of your looks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't feel like people are watching me, talking about me, or targeting me because of how I look. My focus is purely on how bad I think I look in photos and in the mirror, and even though my mom and roommate tell me they don't notice anything wrong, I still strongly believe my nose is huge and crooked and my skin is uneven.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had other unusual beliefs, like being watched, followed, or harmed because of your appearance, or is the concern limited only to your looks and photos?\n\nPatient: No, I have never believed that I was being watched, followed, or harmed in any way. My concerns are strictly limited to my physical appearance and how bad I look in photos.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, such as hearing or seeing things that others do not, or feeling that people are trying to harm or control you?\n\nPatient: No, I have never experienced hearing or seeing things that others do not. I've also never felt like anyone was trying to harm or control me in any way.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think there is a chance your concern about your appearance could be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain the defect is real even when others disagree?\n\nPatient: I feel completely certain that the flaws are real, because when I look in the mirror or at photos, the crookedness of my nose and my uneven skin are just so glaringly obvious. Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers tell me I look fine and that they don't notice anything, I honestly can't believe they don't see it too.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever been able to consider that your appearance concerns might be a false belief or an exaggeration, or are you completely unable to doubt them even a little?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure.
